test_title: PYST 1: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: maths
question: ABC and PQR are two triangles. AB = PQ = 6 cm, BC = QR = 10 cm and AC = PR = 8 cm. If angle ABC = x degree, then what is the value of angle PRQ ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sides 6, 8, and 10 form a Pythagorean triple because 6² + 8² = 10² (36 + 64 = 100).

Thus, both ΔABC and ΔPQR are right-angled triangles with the longest side (10 cm) as the hypotenuse.

In ΔABC, BC is the hypotenuse ⇒ ∠A = 90°. So, ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 90°.

Since the triangles are congruent (SSS rule), ∠PRQ = ∠ACB.

Given ∠ABC = x, then ∠ACB = 90° − x.

**∴ The correct answer is (90 − x) degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: AB = PQ = 6 cm, BC = QR = 10 cm, AC = PR = 8 cm, and ∠ABC = x°.

Formula: In a right-angled triangle, the two acute angles are complementary (sum to 90°).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a1a2c4a62c6294291121e7f3a1e8cb6ea6f66116d2edf8d9f6f1455e25cf559.png] 

⇒ In ΔABC, sides are 6, 8, 10. Check: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100 = 10².

⇒ Since BC² = AB² + AC², ∠BAC = 90°.

⇒ In ΔABC, ∠ABC + ∠ACB + ∠BAC = 180°

⇒ x + ∠ACB + 90° = 180° ⇒ ∠ACB = 90° − x.

⇒ Since AB = PQ, BC = QR, and AC = PR, then ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR (By SSS Congruence Rule).

⇒ Corresponding parts of congruent triangles (CPCT) are equal, so ∠PRQ = ∠ACB.

⇒ ∠PRQ = 90° − x.

**∴ The correct answer is (90 − x) degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

SSS Congruence Rule

If three sides of one triangle are equal to the three sides of another triangle, then the two triangles are congruent.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers (a, b, c) such that a² + b² = c², which always form a right-angled triangle (e.g., 3-4-5, 6-8-10, 5-12-13).

Complementary Angles

In any right-angled triangle, the two non-right angles always add up to 90°, making them complementary to each other.</p
